lines.text: Three men hold a speed record that nobody has broken in more than fifty years.
Tom Stafford, Gene Cernan and John Young: the crew of Apollo 10.
In May 1969, coming home from the Moon, they hit the top of the atmosphere at twenty-four thousand, seven hundred and ninety-one miles an hour.
That's nearly forty thousand kilometres an hour.
No human beings have ever gone faster, relative to the Earth.
So what does hitting the air that fast do to a spacecraft? Find out in the full video. It's linked right here.
